transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-12-26 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Dr. Emily Chen (CTO, Summerset), Carlos Rivera (Head of ML Ops), Maya Singh (Security), Olivia Park (PM)

Summary (auto): Quick walkthrough of rate limiting features, demo of Console org/project key UI, discussion of quotas, burst behavior, and security controls. Agreed next steps for pricing and POC.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Jordan from Redwood, with Priya our SE, we'll run through the org and project key rate limits and how you can control quotas per team.
[00:12] Dr. Emily Chen: Hi thanks, quick context - we're evaluating infra for inference across multiple clinics, we need tenant isolation, cost controls and SOC 2 proof points.
[00:20] Jordan Lee: Totally, that's what we're focused on here. Priya, do you want to start on the console side and then we'll show API examples?
[00:27] Priya Patel: Yep, I'll share my screen. So I'm in the Redwood Console, top left org selector shows Summerset-Org (demo). Under Settings -> Rate Limits we have org-level defaults - these are applied unless a project overrides.
[00:40] Priya Patel: Example: org default token QPS set to 500 RPS, token burst 1000 for short spikes, and per-project quotas to cap monthly token usage. You can see a per-route override for embeddings and streaming endpoints.
[00:55] Carlos Rivera: When you say token QPS, is that per-key or aggregated across the org?
[01:00] Priya Patel: Good question. We support both modes. By default the org quota is aggregated, but you can enforce per-project or per-api-key limits. So you can create project keys for Clinic-A and Clinic-B and give each a 100 RPS hard limit.
[01:14] Maya Singh: And how are those keys scoped? If someone leaks a key, can we rotate without impacting other projects?
[01:20] Priya Patel: Yes, keys are project-scoped. You can rotate at the key-level; we also support short-lived keys and fine-grained RBAC so only certain service accounts can create keys. Rotation is non-disruptive to other project keys.
[01:32] Jordan Lee: I'll add that we also have org-level kill-switch and circuit breaker policies for emergency throttling.
[01:38] Dr. Emily Chen: What about multi-tenant noisy neighbor issues - does Redwood do automatic fallback to dedicated capacity?
[01:45] Priya Patel: We have routing policies. For orgs with Dedicated reservations you can pin certain projects to dedicated nodes, others to hosted. If the dedicated pool hits capacity, we can fallback to a lower-cost hosted variant or apply automatic shedding. There are controls for that - can set priority and SLA tiers.
[02:02] Olivia Park: Can you show how we set per-project monthly quotas? We want to bill clinics separately.
[02:08] Priya Patel: Sure - Projects -> Billing & Quotas -> Create quota. You set a token budget (e.g., 2M tokens/month). When a project hits 90% we emit an alert and optionally block request types or throttle to a lower rate.
[02:23] [screen scroll noise]
[02:30] Priya Patel: Here is the API snippet for creating a project key and attaching a quota: POST /v1/orgs/{org_id}/projects with body project_name and quotas, then the system returns a project_key. In the console we can generate it and mark it as 'ephemeral' or 'permanent'.
[02:45] Carlos Rivera: For the API, do you have SDKs? We want a Python client in our mlops pipelines.
[02:49] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have SDKs for Python, Node, and Go. The SDKs automatically attach project-key headers and handle retries.
[02:56] Dr. Emily Chen: On enforcement, is it token-based (LLM tokens) or request-based? We're doing a mix of short prompts and longer streaming sessions.
[03:03] Priya Patel: We support both. Quotas can be token-based (recommended for cost tracking) and rate-limits are requests/second or tokens/second for streaming. For long streaming sessions we track concurrent sessions plus token throughput.
[03:18] Maya Singh: Quick security question - KMS integration and audit logs.
[03:22] Priya Patel: We support customer-managed keys via major KMS providers and HSM integrations. All key usage and API access events are logged and can be exported to your SIEM; audit logs include project_key id, requester IP, and evaluated policy. Retention is configurable.
[03:37] Carlos Rivera: And SSO? We need SAML/SCIM and role sync.
[03:41] Jordan Lee: Yes SAML SSO with SCIM provisioning and RBAC mapping. You can map groups to project roles (view, manage keys, billing).
[03:50] [brief pause]
[03:58] Priya Patel: Now I'll show a quick demo of throttling behavior. I'm going to run a synthetic load against a project key.
[04:05] [keyboard clacking]
[04:12] Priya Patel: You can see initial throughput at 120 RPS then we cross the project's 100 RPS hard limit; the system returns 429 and an explanatory header x-rd-rate-limit-remaining with info.
[04:25] Carlos Rivera: Is the 429 immediate or do you do graceful degradation? We prefer folding requests into a queue rather than immediate rejects for certain endpoints.
[04:33] Priya Patel: We have both. You can configure a leaky-bucket queue for non-latency-sensitive routes, or strict rejects for interactive latency-sensitive endpoints. You set per-route behavior in the Console.
[04:45] Dr. Emily Chen: Where do we see metrics? We need per-project cost dashboards and token breakdowns by route.
[04:51] Priya Patel: Console -> Analytics -> Per Project. You get token counts, latency p50/p95, and cost estimate per token model. There's also integration with Datadog and Prometheus if you want raw metrics.
[05:05] Jordan Lee: I want to call out Redwood Optimize suggestions - Optimize will recommend batching/quantization per workload and show expected cost savings which can tie into quotas to enforce cost limits.
[05:15] Olivia Park: Is Optimize part of the default product or an add-on?
[05:18] Jordan Lee: It's an add-on; for customers running many projects it usually pays for itself quickly. We'll include pricing in the sheet.
[05:25] Maya Singh: Any gotchas for HIPAA or PII-sensitive data?
[05:29] Priya Patel: We recommend Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for regulated data. For hosted options we provide BAAs, SOC 2 Type II, and optional log redaction; keys and data can be encrypted with your KMS.
[05:42] Dr. Emily Chen: If we go Private or VPC, can we still use org/project keys in the same way?
[05:46] Priya Patel: Yes, the control plane can be customer-managed and you get the same org/project abstractions. The enforcement agent runs in your VPC. Occasionally the product name shows up in docs as Redwood Dedicate - sorry typo - but functionality is identical.
[06:00] [laughter]
[06:05] Carlos Rivera: When we run a POC, we'd like to validate a spike test and a long tail sustained throughput. How do we simulate both?
[06:12] Priya Patel: Provide a sample traffic profile (CSV or JMeter), we can run it against a sandbox org and produce the same metrics you'll see in prod. We'll also show the behavior with a mixed set of project keys to surface noisy neighbor effects.
[06:26] Jordan Lee: For pricing, we bill hosted usage per token with tiered discounts and Dedicated is a reserved capacity contract. We'll send an example with modeling templates to split cost per project.
[06:36] Olivia Park: Can the project-level quotas be used to auto-bill internal teams? We want automated alerts that create a ticket when a team crosses threshold.
[06:44] Priya Patel: Yes - you can attach webhook actions on threshold events (90%, 100%), or create programmatic actions to create tickets in Jira/ServiceNow.
[06:55] Maya Singh: About leakage - if a key is leaked, can we scope an immediate revoke and re-issue? How fast is that enforced?
[06:59] Priya Patel: Revokes are immediate across the CDN edge; the maximum propagation is under a minute in most regions. We also support short-lived tokens for ephemeral jobs.
[07:10] [screen switch]
[07:12] Priya Patel: Here is a policy example: block all embedding endpoints if project exceeds token budget, but keep chat endpoints at reduced rate for critical workflows. We also show logs of which requests were blocked and why.
[07:26] Carlos Rivera: For auditability, does the log show the model version used? We need that for our model governance.
[07:30] Priya Patel: Yes, logs include model id, model checkpoint, prompt hash, and token usage per call. If you pin model versions you can see rollouts and regressions in the Console.
[07:42] Dr. Emily Chen: Any limitations on number of project keys? We plan to create keys per clinic and have thousands.
[07:47] Priya Patel: We support many thousands of keys; recommended pattern is to group by logical unit and use short-lived tokens for per-user sessions to keep management scalable.
[07:58] Jordan Lee: Ok let's talk about the POC scope - validate three things: enforcement correctness (429 vs queue), performance under burst with Dedicated vs hosted fallback, and billing/accounting accuracy.
[08:09] Olivia Park: That sounds right. Timeline? We're hoping to start early Jan.
[08:12] Jordan Lee: We'll aim for POC kickoff week of Jan 9 - Jordan will send pricing and Priya will prep sandbox and scripts. Carlos will provide traffic profile.
[08:21] Maya Singh: One more: data residency - can logs be stored in EU-only? We have EU clinics.
[08:25] Priya Patel: Yes, per-tenant region pinning is supported and logs/data residency controls available on Private or region-isolated hosted tiers.
[08:34] [brief interruptions]
[08:40] Dr. Emily Chen: Great, that addresses most of our compliance questions. Two quick follow ups: can we get a redlined SOC 2 doc, and a sample BAA?
[08:49] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll attach the SOC2 and BAA in the follow-up email.
[08:52] [longer demo jump ahead]
[18:15] Priya Patel: I'm switching to the API demo, here's an example curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer PROJECT_KEY_xxx" -d '{"prompt":"..."}'. Response headers include x-rd-rate-limit-remaining and x-rd-retry-after on 429.
[18:35] Carlos Rivera: If we have internal multiplexers, is there a way to do per-user subquotas?
[18:40] Priya Patel: You can implement sub-scoping within your system and use short-lived tokens per user; Redwood also supports metered tags on requests so you can track per-user usage in logs.
[18:52] Dr. Emily Chen: Will shared caches (prefix/KV cache) affect quota accounting?
[18:56] Priya Patel: Cached responses reduce token usage since the runtime can serve from KV cache; we still account for tokens generated but caches lower total consumption. Note sometimes KV cache is transcribed as KV cash in docs - that's just a transcription issue.
[19:09] Jordan Lee: Quick note on observability - Redwood Console gives token-level cost breakdown and you can drill into a single token request to see latency, model, and whether it hit cache.
[19:20] Carlos Rivera: For our finance people, do you output a monthly export with per-project cost?
[19:24] Priya Patel: Yes CSV export per project and per-route, and you can push to S3.
[19:30] Dr. Emily Chen: Ok great. Any questions from your side, Summerset?
[19:34] Olivia Park: Not right now. We just want a POC to validate limits and check that alerts work for internal billing.
[19:40] Jordan Lee: We'll send the plan. Last thing - are there any blockers for your security team?
[19:46] Maya Singh: Just want the SOC2 and BAA plus confirmation that keys can be rotated and logs exported to our SIEM.
[19:51] Jordan Lee: We'll include those.
[20:00] [wrap up]
[20:05] Jordan Lee: To recap next steps: 1) Jordan send pricing and SOC2/BAA, 2) Priya share sandbox and load scripts, 3) Carlos provide traffic profile, 4) Schedule POC kickoff week of Jan 9.
[20:18] Dr. Emily Chen: Thanks everyone, excited to see the POC.
[20:22] Jordan Lee: Thanks, talk soon.

Notes: transcript contains occasional mis-transcriptions and shorthand typical of call exports. References to product names and features sometimes abbreviated (e.g., Redwood Dedicated -> Redwood Dedicate in chat; KV cache occasionally spelled KV cash).
